summary: Comprehensive end-to-end test of MedFind pharmacy marketplace. Backend: 15/15 pytest assertions pass covering auth (demo login + register), AI chat medication identification, preview-match with AI filter suggestion, blind-view enforcement, watchlist and schedule queue filters, full clarify->reject->AI refinement->accept lifecycle with $4.99 simulated fee and contact exchange, watchlist CRUD, and role-based auth guards. Frontend: verified via Playwright - landing AI chat identifies 'Lipitor 20mg tablets' -> fills Intake Progress (Name/Dose/Form) -> Continue enabled; patient demo login works; New Request submits (free+fill-today shows only 2 matches - AI suggestion appears when count<2); Pharmacy demo login shows KPI strip (4/3/0/1), blind queue (no patient_name/email visible), 3 Watchlist alert badges for Ozempic/Adderall, watchlist-only filter reduces 4->3 rows all bearing alert, Schedule II filter shows only 1 row. Clarify modal + Reject modal work; AI refinement badge appears on refined request. Accept removes row from queue, toast shows $4.99, Accepted tab shows patient contact (name/phone/email). Watchlist add/remove works. Both Concierge buttons (landing and pharmacy) are correctly disabled with 'Coming soon'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py sets cookies with secure=True, samesite='none' - correct for cross-site preview but requires HTTPS (fine for Emergent preview). Frontend uses Bearer token from localStorage as primary auth mechanism which also works.

CORS_ORIGINS='*' combined with allow_credentials=True is technically invalid per spec (browsers ignore credentials with wildcard). Not blocking since frontend uses Authorization header, but for future production, set explicit origins.

seed.py only re-seeds requests/users if patient count is 0. Any tests that mutate seeded requests (e.g., accepting Ozempic) will persist across container restarts; tests are written to create fresh TEST_ requests to avoid cross-run coupling.
ai_service.identify_medication returns 'identified' possibly null or dict; frontend Landing.jsx should handle both (verified working during test - fields populated correctly).
PharmacyDashboard queue-row uses non-testid'd filter labels e.g. filter-Schedule II with a space. Consider kebab-case testids like filter-schedule-ii for robustness.
test_credentials: patient@demo.com/demo123, downtown@demo.com/demo123, greenvalley@demo.com/demo123 - all verified working
seed_data_creation: Backend tests create TEST_-prefixed requests via patient@demo.com; some persist and appear in My Requests tab (expected). No cleanup needed for demo.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 10 requested features validated end-to-end. Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_backend.py (run: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v). Note that clarify-input/reject-input are rendered in Radix Dialog portals - use page-level selectors, NOT queue-row scoped. Filter testids for clinical filters use label with spaces: filter-Schedule II, filter-Schedule III–V (en-dash), filter-Fridge, filter-Specialty.
